CONTRIBUTORY NEGLIGENCE 31.
It is submitted by Ld counsel for respondent insuance company that claimant was himself in violation of law and actively involved in atleast contributory negligence in the present case.
It is further argued that on bare reading of material on record, it is not in dispute that claimant parked his vehicle on road at an anauthorised place.

32. On the other hand, it is denied by Ld. counsel for claimant that there is any contributory negligence on part of claimant.

33. On bare perusal of site plan which is part of charge sheet,
which is filed and relied by claimant only, it can be noted that vehicle of claimant was parked on a main road.
In any case, it is not a parking place.
It is a running traffic road.
Further during cross examination of PW-1/ claimant by insurance company as well as by R-2, claimant himself admitted that he was not aware if the place was an authorised parking place.
Thus, on the basis of material on reocord, it is concluded that there is contributory negligence on the part of claimant also.
And on the facts of present case, it is held that 25 per cent deduction be made on accont of such contributory negligence.
It is ordered accordingly.
34. Thus, after deduction of such 25%, the claim amount of the petitioner would be Rs. 74,362/- (Rs. 99149/- (-) Rs. 24,787/-) .

17. The three-Judge Bench summed up its conclusions and we think it appropriate to reproduce the relevant part of the same: (Swaran Singh case , SCC pp. 341-42, para 110):
"110. (iii) The breach of policy condition e.g. disqualification of the driver or invalid driving licence of the driver, as contained in sub-section (2)(a)(ii) of Section 149, has to be proved to have been committed by the insured for avoiding liability by the insurer.

Mere absence, fake or invalid driving licence or disqualification of the driver for driving at the relevant time, are not in themselves defences available to the insurer against either the insured or the third parties.

To avoid its liability towards the insured, the insurer has to prove that the insured was guilty of negligence and failed to exercise reasonable care in the matter of fulfilling the condition of the policy regarding use of vehicles by a duly licensed driver or one who was not disqualified to drive at the relevant time.

opennyai_summary.issue:
P.NO.3 Of 17 (
 (I) Whether the damaged vehicle bearing no. PB 22M  4040 (Mahindra XUV 500 Car) has suffered damages  in a road traffic accident dated 26.02.2019 involving  vehicle bearing no. HR 66A 0071 (car) being driven by  R-1, owned by R-2 and insured with R-3 due to rash  and negligent driving of R-1, ?
OPP  (II) Whether the owner of the damaged vehicle is  entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and  from whom?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In Cholamandlam Insurance Company Ltd.
Vs. Kamlesh 2009(3) AD-Delhi 310 it was held that if driver does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be Shantanu Arora vs . Mukesh Kumar Singh & Ors.
In National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet u/s 279 IPC is sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
All such three cars were seized by the police officials at that time.
19. It is well settled that the proceedings before the Claims Tribunal are in the nature of inquiry and the finding of rash and negligent driving by driver of the offending vehicle is to be returned only at the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
The factors noted above are sufficient to conclude that preponderance of probability is made out showing negligence of respondent No. 1 in causing the accident.
20. In view of the evidence adduced by claimant in present petition, R-1 did not appear in witness box nor cross examined the claimant and charge-sheet against R1, the issue No. 1 is decided accordingly, in favour of the claimant.
25. Hon'ble Punjab and Haryana High Court in case titled as Amar Singh Vs Ranbir Singh and Ors, 2013 ACJ 1732 held MACT 511/19 Shantanu Arora Vs. Mukesh Kumar Singh & Ors. P.NO.7 Of 17 (r)
 that Tribunal has jurisdiction only to award compensation for actual damage to the vehicle.
26.
27. In the present case, the claimant has proved on recored,
actual bill of Rs. 99,149/- Ex.PW6 paid by him to the authorised workshop for repair of his vehicle.
Further no evidence to contrary placed by respondent side that claimant got reimbursemt from insurance company.
As such, claimant is entitled for such amount in the present claim petition.
28. But as also held in the case law mentioned above, the indirected expenses like money allegedly spent on transportation while victims vehicle was under repair is not tenable.
Further, no proof / evidence is placed on record regarding the claim that he spent rest of the money out of estimate of Rs.
2,10,000/- (apart from Rs. 99,149/-) on repair from other local mechanic, no evidence in this regard placed on record including by examining such local car mechanics or placing on record their bills.
Therefore, just because a estimate of Rs. 2,10,000/- given initially by th workshop the same is not sufficient to proof the actual expenses suffered are the same.
It is further submited that Shantanu Arora vs . Mukesh Kumar Singh & Ors.
37. At this stage, it is pertinent to refer to the case decided by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Amrit Paul Singh And Another Vs.
Tata Aig General Insurance Company Limited And Others .
[
(2018) 7 Supreme Court Cases 558 : (2018) 3 Supreme Court Cases (Cri) 255 :(2018) 3 Supreme Court Cases (Civ) 677 : 2018 Scc Online Sc 548]. In such case it was held :
 ''.......................................In this regard, Sections  2(28) and 2(31) of the Act that define "motor  vehicle" or "vehicle" and "permit" are reproduced  below:
 "2. (28) "motor vehicle" or "vehicle" means  any mechanically propelled vehicle adapted  for use upon roads whether the power of MACT 511/19 Shantanu Arora Vs. Mukesh Kumar Singh & Ors. P.NO.10 Of 17 (r)
 propulsion is transmitted thereto from an  external or internal source and includes a  chassis to which a body has not been  attached and a trailer; but does not include a  vehicle running upon fixed rails or a vehicle  of a special type adapted for use only in a  factory or in any other enclosed premises or  a vehicle having less than four wheels fitted  with engine capacity of not  exceeding twenty-five cubic centimetres;
 .
.
Use of a vehicle in a public place without a permit is a fundamental statutory infraction.

41. Accordingly, in view of the settled law including the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Amrit Paul Singh And Another Vs.
Tata Aig General Insurance Company Limited And Others . [ (2018) 7 Supreme Court Cases 558 : (2018) 3 Supreme Court Cases (Cri) 255 :(2018) 3 Supreme Court Cases (Civ) 677 : 2018 Scc Online Sc 548], the compensation will be payable in the first instance by the insurance company/ R-3, but with liberty to recover the same from the R-1 & R-2.
